title: How Can I Erase My Identity and Start Over?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a news item about New Zealand's law restricting baby names (examples include Tallula Does The Hula From Hawaii, Midnight Chardonnay, Number 16 Bus Shelter, Fish and Chips twins), then discuss whether a person can erase their identity and start over. They explain that in the US, with computer records and paper trails, fully erasing identity is very hard without government help; legal routes include a name change through a court (usually cheap, advertised in a county legal organ, objections possible, as with Jeff Gillooly seeking to become Jeff Stone) and changing a Social Security number under special circumstances such as identity theft misuse or domestic violence. They mention the old "paper trail" trick of assuming a dead infant's identity, Radovan Karadzic hiding in plain sight before his arrest, and scam name-change websites. The episode closes with the SSA phone number and a teaser about albinism and the song "Frankenstein" by Edgar Winter.
topics: starting over with a new identity

segments.title: Opening banter and New Zealand baby name law
segments.summary: Hosts open with casual banter, then discuss New Zealand's law barring overly long or socially handicapping baby names, with examples of names that were and were not allowed, and Chuck's own name origin.

segments.title: Can you erase your identity?
segments.summary: Josh poses the question of how to erase one's identity and start over. They answer that completely erasing identity in the US is very hard without government help because of computer records; the old paper trail trick of using a dead infant's identity is no longer practical.

segments.title: Legal name and Social Security number changes
segments.summary: They explain legal routes: a court name change that is usually cheap and advertised in the county legal organ, with objections possible, and changing a Social Security number when someone is misusing it or in cases of domestic violence. They discuss the Jeff Gillooly name change objection case.

segments.title: Famous identity changes and name change scams
segments.summary: They cite Radovan Karadzic, who hid in plain sight in Belgrade before his arrest, as an example of changing identity to evade war crimes charges. They warn that many internet name-change services are scams and comment that identity theft may be driving more identity changes.

segments.title: SSA contact information
segments.summary: Chuck gives the Social Security Administration phone number for questions about changing a Social Security number and directs listeners to the article for details.

segments.title: Article teaser and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts tease an article on albinism, linked to the song Frankenstein by Edgar Winter, and close with the show's contact email and an ad.
